log: Interface text and structure only, no algorithm or constant changed. One card for the four kinds of finds (shift between passes, track inside a pass, distant body, change of brightness in place): the same rows in the same order (kind, place, time, the two signal-to-noise values, the bar and the control, the colour, the distance with its interval, the catalogues at the place, and for a distant body the state of the WISE archive check: not run, it is asked for candidates seen in D4 only); the track of the film and the peaks of the distance search got the card the lead and the pair already had. Distance, own motion and the pass of the distance search are in the address. The wording of what a blind search can reach is a status line in every result of the search beyond Neptune: about V 20–21 in reflected light, and a margin of 1.4–1.7× over the WISE Planet Nine search only in D4 (3 µm). Dead code removed from the page (the unused modal, two projection helpers, the old mosaic remnants and some unused constants).

Display and interface, no pipeline value changed. (1) Reference: a small static picture of the same square of sky from an old survey (Pan-STARRS i first, then DSS2, 2MASS, WISE; the archive images the page already fetches), grey, survey and year written on it, a ring on the selected source, in the corner of the picture; a Display switch, a click for the next survey; it is for rejecting artefacts by looking at both, not a measurement. (2) Stretch: the asinh “linear” parameter (the soft knee; default = the law’s own, 0.4) and the trim of the white point: fixed (400, as before), the 99.5th or 99.9th percentile of the field’s own unsaturated white-light pixels (every second pixel of every pass), or adaptive (99.9th percentile × 1.15); all never above the fixed level; the defaults give exactly the earlier picture. (3) Film: “Trail” draws the last three places of each found track, fading; “Blink” shows five cut-outs of the same piece of sky (the middle of the chosen track) in five of the visits the track was found in, unmarked, the visit on screen outlined; “Film around this track” reads the field again, 10′ or 20′ wide, centred on the middle place of the track, and opens the film of the same pass. (4) The address carries the frame (when paused), the speed (0.25× to 4×, also for the films), the selected source or place and the open panel, the film (pass, frame, mode, candidates, trail, blink, track), the reference and the stretch; Copy link writes them first. The flip speed of the pendulum and of the films is one control. (5) Movers: the line “between passes” also says “chance n”, the number of tracks (and of pairs changing in place) that chance alone makes in a field like this, from a control of the same search on moved sources (60 trials); it is the service’s number, shown as it is. (6) Globe: while a survey has no data yet at the centre of the view, the last picture that had data stays, scaled to the new zoom, instead of a black canvas.

Display: Sharpen rebuilt and on by default. The old unsharp mask (negative lobe, 55 % floor, switched off beside saturated pixels) drew contour blobs round bright stars, darkened haloes, red rims at saturated cores and red specks at 10′–60′, so it had been left off. The new one only boosts: gain = 1 + 16 · t² / (t + 0.1), t = (L − blur) / L taken on the white-light layer of the pass (the layer the quick stage already has, so the quick stage, partial passes, Difference, Co-add, the walls and any band selection take the same path), multiplied equally into every layer and channel before the display law, so the colour cannot change. The gain is zero where L is under 3 σ of the pass’s own noise (median and 1.4826 MAD of every third pixel) and full from 8 σ, zero at and fading smoothly over 1–3 detector pixels (6.2″) away from a saturated pixel or a pixel without data in any layer (a distance map made when the pass arrives), and tapered to zero as the stretched value rises from 0.12 to 0.4, so bright stars are left alone. The blur radius is one detector pixel (7.7″) in grid pixels, between 1.5 and 5. Audited on the 5 test targets × 2′/5′/10′/20′/60′ × every pass (ui_sharp_audit.md): no red isolated cell, no extra isolated bright cell, no channel mean moved by more than 1.0/255, at most 2.2 % of the cells changed by more than 20/255, no contour ray beyond the off picture. It makes faint stars brighter and crisper (peak +16 % to +164 %; FWHM −24 % at 2′ in the best case, unchanged at 20′ and 60′ where the grid is one detector pixel); it does not narrow bright stars.

Interface text and one display rule. Pair of sources: when the search between passes finds a track whose peak hops between two cores while the light-weighted centre hardly moves, the lab shows no mover but a ring round the pair and a card (the verdict, the flux of each core per pass, their ratio, the change by detector, a zoom of 4× or more). Anomaly passport: “Anomaly n” with the bins that drive its score in words, the residual of every bin on the charts, and what SIMBAD, Gaia, 2MASS, AllWISE, CatWISE, VSX and NED know about the place (a catalogue that did not answer is said). Spectrum tab: a source saturated in every exposure has no SPHEREx spectrum and says so once; WISE 0855 is shown binned in wavelength with 3σ upper limits as arrows. Archive images on the timeline take part in the marker, the trajectory (the proper motion carried back to the plate), the speed rings (the longest span), the camera on the object and the playback. Colour: the white balance is taken per pass from that pass’s own field stars (a typical star’s balance in the detectors that looked at the field where there are fewer than six), one saturation for the whole field. Sharper stacks (service e34): each native pixel is spread over the grid with a Gaussian of 0.35 detector pixel when at least 16 exposures stand in the stack, 0.50 when fewer do; the stacks are shown smoothed with 0.5 grid pixel; stars in the white frame are 9.2 arcsec wide at half maximum (10.7 before).

Interface text only: Movers is one row of the Searches list that summarises every search for moving bodies of the field, each started by itself when the field is ready and shown with its status and bar: between passes (years), inside a pass (days; the film), inside a visit (hours, fields up to 10′); one result line per scale (“1 track”, “no track”, “no fast body”). A track shows what Gaia says (same motion / stands still, rejected and not drawn / no Gaia star / not checked yet); a track whose Gaia check is not done is drawn dashed and labelled “unchecked”, never as a confirmed mover.

Interface text only, no algorithm changed: a click selects a source of the field’s own list (S/N 7 or more or saturated; stars and unknown sources alike), the catalogue only names it; the named target says “Not detected” when no source stands at its predicted place (WISE 0855) and gives no change verdict on noise; the spectrum is drawn point by point while it is measured; Movers is a row of the Searches list; one Marker switch; the progress bars and the spectral-anomalies button.

Display: Sharpen is on by default in the lab (the Display switch turns it off). An unsharp mask of the real pixels in linear flux, before the display law: radius 5 grid pixels, amount 4, the blur taken over valid unsaturated pixels, nothing sharpened within one detector pixel of a saturated core, the result never below 55 % of the local value; in the colour picture the mask acts on the luminance, so no colour rim appears. Measured at 5′ and 20′: the on-screen FWHM of isolated stars falls by 1–2″ (the floor is the stack, 10.4″) and the faint stars (S/N 5–14) that reach a visible brightness grow from 4 to 12 of 12 at 5′ and from 11 to 25 of 308 at 20′. No new data is made.

The sum of the passes along one orbit is begun (work in progress): engine/deepsum.py, /api/field_deep with a plan call that gives the number of orbits and the estimate of the time before the job starts, a lab block. The numbers for Sedna are not yet part of the page.

Find Planet X in one pass: /api/field_distant and engine/distant.py (the port of px.py): visit images on 3.075″, the static sky from the other passes, the scan of distance and own motion with the negated-differences ceiling, refinement of the place on the unclipped differences, photometry along the track and control tracks; a distance slider in the lab (shift and add on the CPU). Eris found blind in the pass of July 2025 (12.0σ, 96.4 au, 0.072 mJy). The sum of the passes along one orbit is not built yet.

The anomaly map in the lab: /api/field_anomaly and engine/anomaly.py (the port of anomaly.py), a background job on a finished field that measures every source that stands still at S/N 12 and every track in every exposure and compares the binned spectra with an ordinary star of the field (median shape and two principal components); rings only above median + 6 robust sigma; a card with the spectrum over the fit. On ε Indi at 20′ the brown dwarf ε Indi B is the strongest by far.

The search inside a pass is verified and linked with an orbit model: on − off PSF photometry of the film’s candidates (OUTLIER kept for bodies, references from every pass, two stages as in fast.verify), the orbit model of the offline search (engine/orbit.py) with the telescope’s own motion, a track needs 5σ together, recovery along the orbit on the motion maps, the scrambled control, SkyBoT. (9078) 1994 PB2 is linked by the orbit (3.5 au, residual 0.37″); Orwell is not (its third candidate is 2.0σ, and a 1σ bar fails the control). The spectrum of a moving body keeps OUTLIER pixels.

The film of one pass is in the lab (section “The film of one pass”): one frame per visit (the median of its exposures, OUTLIER pixels kept), aligned, motion only against the median of the visits of the same detector with static sources masked; candidates of 6σ linked along straight lines (4″, scatter ≤ 1.5″), recovered on the motion maps, drawn only when a scrambled control says chance makes fewer than 0.15 such tracks per field, then checked against SkyBoT. On the ecliptic test field (20′, December 2025) it found (9078) 1994 PB2 blind; (11020) Orwell is visible in the film but not linked (its path bends). No photometric verification and no orbit model yet.

Stage 4 carry-over and the search between passes in the lab: the detector wall counts a detector whose fits had a masked core (a saturated star) against a 1.5″ floor and subtracts each detector’s own registration residual (Barnard’s Star reads 6 of 6 again, for a stated reason); the spectrum of a named object starts with the field; the zoom inset is a quarter of the width and sits in the corner farthest from the object; the thermal line is in the card of a known body. The search between passes (engine/search.py, the port of detect.py) runs on the white stacks of every finished field with at least three passes, followed by a Gaia check; tracks are drawn only when found, with a card, the same place in every pass and the spectrum along the track.

Stage 4 of the lab: the spectrum of a clicked place or the named target is measured by the service (PSF fit on a 7 × 7 stamp, VARIANCE weights, three rounds of 6σ rejection, neighbours in wavelength) on a small window around the object in every exposure, at every field size; the aperture sum is removed; a saturated object gets no calibrated spectrum and says so; the Object card’s change test uses the new points. New: the check against 2MASS and AllWISE (synthetic photometry under the filter curves), the portrait (56 layers by wavelength around the object, co-moving, and a colour thumbnail), the on − off spectrum of a moving body and the thermal ratio in its card, and the time machine (up to twelve archive images by date, sky fixed or camera on the object), which replaces the single AllWISE image.

Stage 3 fix round: the build of a field streams (sums per pass and detector, the leave-one-out test against the sums minus the exposure’s own deposit, registration by a spline shift on pass 0), all overlapping exposures at every size (60′ of Barnard’s Star: 603, was 105), service memory 1.1 GB at 60′ (macOS allocator set to return freed memory); the viewer gets the picture part (colour, as float16) pass by pass and the detector, band and Difference parts when their view opens (60′: 33 MB instead of 190–385 MB); the next pass is read while one is stacked. The text about mosaics and seams is gone from the Method page.

The search for bodies beyond Neptune is updated to its fourth step (sections “Find Planet X”, now six). Second version: a cleaner static sky (clipped mean over all other passes), a mask margin that grows with the brightness, the sum scaled by its own spread: 60–75 times fewer false peaks, almost no gain in depth. Third version: the visits of all passes added along one orbit, then PSF photometry of the 100 strongest peaks of the sum and of the negated sum, the threshold set by the negated peaks: Sedna (V 20.8) found blind at 9.1σ, distance 82.9 au (JPL 83.0); blind limit 0.034 mJy. Fourth step: detector D4 alone with a prior for orbits like Planet Nine and a test with artificial bodies: the blind limit at 3 µm is 1.4–1.7 times deeper than the WISE search; one candidate at 394 au was ruled out with ten years of WISE exposures along its orbit. Code in `motion_pipeline/px`; not in the lab yet (status table).

Stage 3 of the lab: field sizes 2′, 5′, 10′, 20′ and 60′ (were 3′, 6′, 12′, 24′, 36′), one request for every size, from the exposures that overlap the field; the mosaics of 12′ cubes are gone; wide fields are built from a selection that fits in memory; wavelength-dependent background from 10′ up; no per-visit test above 12′; a Display option “Speed rings” (1, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300 ″/yr, r = v·Δt between the first and the last pass). The coverage preview of the globe accepts every size (it answered 400 above 12′).

Difference is calibrated on the data: the noise term of z is multiplied by the robust width of (D − S)/σ measured locally on empty sky (before: ε Indi B pass 3 showed 11.9 % of the field above |z| = 4, now 0.9 % and a single pair at the target; width of z on empty sky 2.2–4.4 before, 0.93–1.05 now on the white frame). Wall layouts use the whole area (columns chosen by the aspect ratio, rows centred). The wall of detectors compares each detector with the catalogue shift. The status line says when a pass has no exposures in some detectors. Globe: the order-3 Allsky image is slightly smoothed; HEALPix tile orientation verified against Orion, Crux and the Pleiades.

Stage 2 of the lab. Views: the single picture, the wall of bands (the former Split: seven named panels) and the wall of detectors (six panels with words, D1–D6, microns, the shift of the target per detector and “N of 6 agree”), each with its own address value (view=). Difference is computed in the viewer from the pass stacks with the formula of section “Difference between passes and the artifact mask”, for fields up to 12′. The artifact mask is a Display checkbox with a hover tooltip that names the flags of the pixel (a flag census of the exposures is built by the service). The display options (follow the target, brighten, zoom, interpolate, ring, trail, saturated cores white) work in the new viewer. The splat of the stacks deposits each native pixel bilinearly on four grid points and smooths once (sigma 0.50 detector pixel), and the quick frame is shown in white light only. Globe: backgrounds Dust map, Optical — DSS2, Near-infrared — 2MASS, Infrared — WISE from the IRSA HiPS mirror.

A third search is part of the method: bodies beyond Neptune, too faint for one exposure (three sections “Find Planet X”). Inside one pass the visit differences are added along trial distances (30–300 au, or 250–2000 au) and own motions, the threshold is the height that noise alone reaches, and every candidate is checked by PSF photometry on the exposures and by control tracks; between passes one two-body orbit through the tracks gives the distance from the parallax jump. Tested blind on Eris and Makemake (found in 3 of 3 passes each, distance within 0.6 % of JPL), on Sedna (below the blind limit, 10σ along its known track), and on the field of the IRAS/AKARI Planet Nine candidate (nothing confirmed). Code in `motion_pipeline/px`. Not in the lab yet (status table).

Super-frames, pendulum and spectral color are in the lab for fields up to 12′: the service builds the stacks with the engine (native pixels, leave-one-out and per-visit tests, registration, saturated share, white frame over the detectors present in every pass, seven named-band stacks), the browser draws them in WebGL. Splat kernel 0.30 → 0.50 detector pixel (the lattice of the pass difference, see Super-frames step 3). The cosmic-ray test protects sources that the other exposures see. Measured by the application on Barnard’s Star: 10.40 ± 0.13 ″/yr from 361 exposures (the catalogue gives 10.41 over the same interval); ε Indi B: 4.55 ± 0.03 ″/yr from 447 exposures in four passes (catalogue 4.58). Exposures at the edge of the detector (Barnard’s Star within 8 pixels of it) enter the stacks but not the fit of the position.

The Method page is rewritten as one account of the method. New in it: the raw frames as the baseline; super-frames (stacking with super-resolution on a 1.54″ grid, the leave-one-out test for cosmic-ray hits, the per-visit test for streaks, the contrast rule for halos); what is marked on a picture; the test fields; pendulum, spectral color, the wall of six detectors, nested fields and five field sizes, archive images; the object portrait and the PSF-fit spectrum with its check against 2MASS and WISE; the search between passes; the spectrum along a track and the blind search with an orbit model on the ecliptic field; the anomaly map and the thermal ratio; challenge items, service and tools. These steps are implemented in `motion_pipeline/` and were run on three fields; the status table in section 1 says what the lab computes today for each. The descriptions of the lab’s field grid and mosaics, its co-add and its display options left the page (the status table names them; the full text is in the M15 version of this file); the Difference view and the artifact mask keep theirs in a section of their own. **No algorithm or constant of the lab changed in this version.** The sky service and its cache moved into this project (`service/`).

Parallax of the spacecraft in the linker (six trial distances, Eros 433 is now found by the blind search) and in Investigate (SkyBoT positions moved to the spacecraft’s viewpoint by the service). The seed lines are accepted with three separate epochs when at least 9 detections have a scatter of 0.6 px or less. The artificial sources of the stack use the same static sky as the stack (the exposures within 1.4 h left out). The Investigate rule “probably” is for comets, interstellar objects and orbit errors above 30″ only, with the offset along the track; a match that exists only through the orbit error gets the weak verdict; bodies fainter than V 20 are ignored except near-Earth objects; saved candidates are no longer re-saved (a comment had swallowed the flag) and a field whose SkyBoT query failed saves none. Completeness by rate (window.__lab.syn(levels, K, seed, rate)): see the table in section 7.

Review round 10. A band shown alone on a saturated target no longer says “not seen in this band” (its S/N is 0 by construction); a band with no exposure in the season on show is told apart (“no exposure in this band this season”). The “probably” verdict of Investigate is only for comets and bodies with a large orbit error, and the offset from the track must stay constant (25″) over the three epochs (a track 100″ from Eugenia is no longer “probably Eugenia”); the candidate card, the known-body card and the report follow the result of the check; the report lists the measured positions and the right observer and DOIs. A selected trace in a season is drawn with a white halo; the film’s time ticks are rebuilt when you leave Movers; the globe checks the stored selection against the aim when it opens. Comets without a magnitude are shown as “magnitude n/a”, not V 0.0; SBDB class codes in words; albedo to three digits; the search waits up to 3 minutes for the Gaia list and says so when it did not (a possible cause of the differences some reviewers saw in the Findings rows). The Eros explanation, the RW Aur speed note and the references were corrected.

Review round 9. A bug in the lab: caches keyed by the field version (saturation, motion layer, inset) were reused at another scale, so after switching 6′ → 3′ → 12′ with the buttons Barnard’s Star showed its motion backwards and lost its saturation note; the version is unique per field now and the caches are cleared with the field. Burst consistency uses 2 (G − 2) degrees of freedom (it had underestimated the scatter of 3-detection bursts, which rejected bright true tracks). Completeness test with a realistic model (scatter 0.2 + 2.5 / S/N px, detection probability 0.35 + 0.04 × S/N): peak S/N 6: 5 of 6, 8, 10, 15 and 30: 6 of 6; false tracks by shuffling after this change: 0 of 8 for Eugenia. Investigate: bodies fainter than V 20 are ignored, the tolerance includes the spacecraft’s parallax and the orbit error, the direction is compared, a weaker “probably” verdict for comets (all three epochs within 120″, rate within 10 %, direction within 10°); the report names the observer and says that the positions are points on the fitted line. The candidate list is read again on every change (two tabs share it); a candidate is saved only when the service answered completely. A clicked moving object has a white ring that follows it. The globe no longer names an object the aim has left. Findings rows re-run with M13: identical to M12; the stated spread between independent runs is now on the page.

Review round 8. Flag value 4 is soft in the film and the stack as it already was in the blind search (3I/ATLAS: the stack peak, 5 px off, is now at the predicted position). The linker refits its best seed lines on their members and gathers again (synthetic faint movers of 22–28 detections at peak S/N 8 and 10 are recovered in 5 of 6 and 6 of 6 trials, at peak S/N 15 in 6 of 6 and at 30 in 4 of 6, where the round-8 review found 0 of 6 for the earlier linker at S/N 8 and 10; the synthetic movers are added to the real candidate detections of the Eugenia field, scatter 0.45 px at every level, reproduced with window.__lab.syn([8,10,15,30], 6) in the console) and stops after two rejected lines. Motion only: the static sky of each exposure leaves out the exposures within 1.4 h. Saturated target: a pixel of the 3 × 3 around it in ANY season counts (the Barnard’s Star comparison inset showed the motion backwards); the diamonds are coloured by season and dated. A solo band is what the comparison inset shows, with its name; a ring in a band where the target is not seen is dashed grey. A target with a catalogued star on its path (WISE 0855) gets no measured motion. RW Aur uses its own SIMBAD motion, not its companion’s. The exported video has the zoom insets. Findings rows re-measured. Globe readout moved into the flow under the coverage key; aria-pressed / aria-current fixed. The stack wording no longer says “clear signal”.

Moving objects can be clicked: a card for a known body (SkyBoT, JPL SBDB) or a candidate; a spectrum along the track; unknown tracks are saved in a candidate list (Findings) with an investigation (SkyBoT within 120″ at three epochs, Gaia on the path) and a report; new service endpoint /api/skybot_cone. The globe no longer changes its scale when an object is shown: it only turns to bring the object into view.

The ring, the trail and the dates in a mosaic (24′, 36′) were drawn in the middle of the mosaic instead of at the target (every cube reported its own centre as the target; now only the cube requested on the target is used); checked on 5 targets × 5 scales against the cores and 283 Gaia stars. Zoom on the target: a magnified crop and a first-versus-last-season comparison (cyan and orange) in a corner of the video.
M9

Review round 6: the star-cluster rule exempts only true saturated regions (a bright unsaturated body was kept inside a star cluster); static sources need two separate epochs; the exclusion zone of a saturated pixel scales with its area; flag 4 (source mask) is soft in the search; the Gaia veto is 0.9 px; the matched filter threshold rises until the negative image has at most one peak; bright tight lines may scatter 0.6 px; the stack has no star masks, an empirical significance from 40 control paths and fake sources added to the pixels; Horizons failure is shown; comet magnitudes are labelled T; labels flip near the edge; timeline labels sit at their slider stops; the Moving objects text is its own section; RW Aur distance on Findings; Findings numbers are produced by this version.

Matched filter for faint sources with its threshold on the measured scatter and the negative image as the false-alarm count; stack along the ephemeris of a named body with a null of far offsets and fake sources on a control path (Movers panel).
